research_rationale: The held official Federal Register text (67 FR 1599, FR Doc. 02-918, filed 2002-01-10 and published 2002-01-11) was read in full and is the order signed 2001-12-28 by President Bush: its heading is Executive Order 13251 of December 28, 2001, Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of State. It sets an order of succession for acting Secretary of State under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998, with four sections: the succession rule, the list of offices, exceptions and the revocation of EO 12343. The 38-clause inventory covers the preamble, each section, each lettered entry and each numbered item and was confirmed against the text. The order has no own-terms end. EO 13261 sec. 4(i) replaced sec. 3(b) on 2002-03-19 and is attached as a later event on that clause. The Office of the Federal Register catalogue lists the order as revoking EO 12343 and as amended by EO 13261 and lists no revocation; the held-text number search found the order cited by EO 13261, by the original copy of itself and in a 2010 Federal Register notice that gives its authority wrongly as EO 13251 for a commission established by a different order. All operative clauses rest on the held original plus these bounded searches through 2026-10-14; the U.S. Code search covers editions current through 2026-10-09, so a law enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 is not reflected.
savings_reason: EO 13251 has no savings, exemption or transitional clause. Its only revocation, sec. 4 of EO 12343, has no proviso preserving anything under the revoked order, and the only held instrument that acts on EO 13251, EO 13261, replaces sec. 3(b) alone and contains no provision preserving or ending rights under it.
earlier_end_check: Searched every held text for the number 13251: the citing texts are EO 13261 (the amendment of sec. 3(b)), the order itself and a 2010 notice establishing the Presidential Commission for the Study of Bioethical Issues whose authority line names Executive Order 13251 with the date November 24, 2009; that date is not the date of this order (December 28, 2001), so the citation is a mistaken reference for that commission and says nothing about this order. The catalogue of Office of the Federal Register disposition notes shows only EO 13261 and no revocation or supersession. The order has no stated end. No earlier end was found.
scope_check: Each of the 38 clauses was read as a separate command or entry. The succession rule, the list entries, the exceptions in sec. 3(a), (c) and (d) and the amended sec. 3(b) are standing provisions that apply when a vacancy occurs and are not exhausted by use. The only performed command is the revocation of EO 12343 in sec. 4. EO 13261 changed only sec. 3(b).
independent_command_check: Sec. 4 (revoking EO 12343) is independent of the succession rule: its performance on 2001-12-28 exhausted it without affecting the rest. The list entries depend on sec. 1 and sec. 3 for their effect but are separate designations; sec. 3(d) keeps them working when an office is renamed. No clause is made conditional on another ending.
savings_check: No clause preserves actions, rights or proceedings, so a later instrument has nothing to leave in place; the only later instrument, EO 13261, replaces sec. 3(b) and has no savings language touching this order.

research_rationale: The held official Federal Register text of EO 13265 (67 FR 39841, FR Doc. 02-14807, published 2002-06-11) was read in full. It establishes the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports, assigns the Secretary of Health and Human Services a purpose (sec. 1), sets membership (sec. 2), functions (sec. 3), administration (sec. 4) and general provisions (sec. 5), with a two-year termination unless extended and the revocation of EO 12345. The 25-clause inventory (each section and each lettered subsection) was confirmed against the text. Sections 1 through 5 were revised to read as follows three times (EO 13545 in 2010, held only as a presidency-project mirror capture of its text, EO 13824 in 2018 and EO 14327 in 2025), and EO 14048 amended the 2018 text in 2021; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 each clause continues, amended, while the order continues, and each revision is a later event on each clause with the substance change disclosed. The contingent two-year end in sec. 5(b) has not occurred because the President extended the Council by the biennial continuation orders from EO 13316 (2003) to EO 14354 (2025), which continues it until 2027-09-30 and lists the Council as established by EO 13265 as amended. Sec. 5(c) revoked EO 12345 once, on signing. The Office of the Federal Register catalogue lists EO 13316, EO 13385, EO 13545, EO 13824 and EO 14327 as amending and the continuation orders as continuing the order, and lists no revocation. The held text of EO 14045 (signed 2021-09-13) is the order on the White House Initiative on Advancing Educational Equity for Hispanics; the character span at which the dossier records an amendment of EO 13265 in that file holds that order's own text about its working group and not an amendment of EO 13265, so EO 14045 is not used and EO 14048 sec. 7 is the 2021 amendment. The U.S. Code search covers editions current through 2026-10-09, so a law enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 is not reflected.
savings_reason: EO 13265 has no savings clause. Its only revocation, sec. 5(c) of EO 12345, carries no proviso preserving anything under the revoked order. The later instruments that revise the order (EO 13545, EO 13824, EO 14327 and EO 14048) contain no provision preserving or ending rights under the original text beyond their own general provisions, which state that nothing in them impairs the authority of departments or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.

research_rationale: The held official Federal Register text of EO 13303 (68 FR 31931, FR Doc. 03-13412, published 2003-05-28) was read in full. It declares a national emergency over the threat of judicial process against the Development Fund for Iraq and Iraqi petroleum, prohibits attachment and similar process against them (sec. 1), carves the property out of EOs 12722, 12724 and 13290 (sec. 2), defines terms (sec. 3), authorises the Treasury to implement (sec. 4) and has the usual disclaimers. The 16-clause inventory covers the opening paragraphs, each section and each lettered definition and was confirmed against the text. Sec. 1 and its subsections ended on 2014-05-27 when EO 13668 terminated the sec. 1 prohibitions as amended by EO 13364, a termination that by its own words left the national emergency in place. The emergency is continued each May by a notice: all 23 notices from 2004 to 2026 are held and attached as later events to the lead clause, the last signed 2026-05-04, which carries the emergency past 2026-05-22 and so through 2026-10-14. The Office of the Federal Register catalogue lists the order as amended by EO 13364 with no revocation. The U.S. Code search covers editions current through 2026-10-09, so a law enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 is not reflected. The authority statutes (IEEPA, the National Emergencies Act, the United Nations Participation Act) are cited in the order and referred to in the 2026 notice as the basis of the continued emergency; no held source shows any of them repealed or expired.
savings_reason: EO 13303 has no savings clause of its own. Its sec. 2(b) preserves administrative action taken under EOs 12722, 12724 and 13290 or under IEEPA and the UNPA. EO 13350 later revoked EO 12722 and EO 12724 and, in its sec. 1, continued the prohibitions on property blocked under them, and EO 13668 terminated the sec. 1 prohibitions with a statement that the national emergency remains in place, so the continuing effects of the order are carried by the emergency, by its continuation notices and by the implementing authority, which is why the savings state is transferred or accrued.
conflict_resolutions: {"PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER":"The five candidate partial ends are resolved as follows. The two EO 13668 entries and the entry dated 2014-05-27 are the one instrument, EO 13668 sec. 1 (signed 2014-05-27), which terminates the prohibitions in sec. 1 of EO 13303 as amended by EO 13364; it is recorded as the first end of the clauses EO:13303#sec1, #sec1-a and #sec1-b and it states that the national emergency declared in EO 13303 remains in place, so it ends no other clause. The entries dated 2005-05-19 and 2006-05-18 are the annual continuation notices of those years; the word terminate in them recounts the President's decision to terminate the national emergency declared in EO 12722 and says the exercise of EO 13290 continues under the EO 13303 emergency, so they end nothing in EO 13303 and are attached as continuation events on the lead clause."}
earlier_end_check: Searched every held text for the number 13303 and the catalogue of Office of the Federal Register disposition notes. The ending instruments are EO 13364 (amends sec. 1, 2004-11-29), EO 13350 (revokes the orders named in sec. 2, effective 2004-07-30) and EO 13668 (terminates sec. 1, 2014-05-27); no earlier revocation or supersession of the order or of its emergency exists in the held texts, and every annual continuation notice from 2004 to 2026 is held. The Notice of May 4, 2026, is the latest and continues the emergency for one year beyond 2026-05-22.
scope_check: Each of the 16 clauses was read separately. Sec. 1, 1(a) and 1(b) are the judicial-process prohibition and ended on 2014-05-27. The opening declaration of the emergency, the carve-out and preservation clauses in sec. 2, the definitions, the Treasury authorisation, the licensing rule and the disclaimers have no end in any held source and are recorded as operative; sec. 2 is noted as narrowed by EO 13350, and sec. 6 is a performed transmittal direction recorded as operative only because the text continues.
independent_command_check: The sec. 1 prohibition and the emergency declaration are independent commands: EO 13668 ended the prohibition and said in the same instrument that the emergency stays in place, so the end of sec. 1 does not end the lead clause, sec. 4 or the definitions that serve them. The sec. 2 carve-out depended on the sec. 1 property description but was not itself ended by 13668.
savings_check: Sec. 2(b) is the only preservation clause. The held later instruments (EO 13350 sec. 1 and EO 13668) either continue the prohibitions on property blocked under the revoked orders in their own text or expressly leave the emergency in place; none revokes sec. 2(b).

research_rationale: The held official Federal Register text (68 FR 44851, FR Doc. 03-19572, filed 2003-07-30) was read in full and is the order signed 2003-07-25 by President Bush: its heading is Executive Order 13309 of July 25, 2003, and its five sections rename the President’s Committee on Mental Retardation, amend EO 12994 and continue the committee until 2005-09-30. The clause inventory of five sections was confirmed against the text and covers every operative sentence. Sections 1 to 4 are amending commands whose results are carried in the current text of EO 12994, which the 42 U.S.C. 15001 note (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints as amended by EO 13309 and EO 13446 sec. 5; EO 13446 restated EO 12994 effective 2007-09-30 and is attached as a later event to each of those clauses. Section 5 ended on its own stated date. The bounded searches named below (U.S. Code, eCFR and the Office of the Federal Register catalogue) were read for coverage: the U.S. Code search covers editions current through 2026-10-09, so a law enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 is not reflected; the catalogue and the number search of the held texts found no revocation, supersession or further amendment of EO 13309 itself.
savings_reason: EO 13309 contains no savings, exemption or transitional clause: its sections 1 to 5 rename a committee, amend EO 12994 and continue the committee until 2005-09-30, and it has no provision preserving pending actions or continuing a prior arrangement. The only later instrument that acts on it in the held evidence, EO 13446, restates EO 12994 and neither revokes EO 13309 nor preserves or reserves any right under it.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts for the number 13309: only the order itself (two copies) cites it, and the catalogue search of Office of the Federal Register disposition notes found no revocation, supersession or termination of EO 13309; the only instrument acting on it through its parent is EO 13446 sec. 5, a restatement of EO 12994 effective 2007-09-30 that is recorded as a later event, not an end. The one own-terms date, 2005-09-30 in sec. 5, is the end of that clause only.
scope_check: Sections 1 to 4 carry out the rename and the amendments of EO 12994; each is treated as continuing in the amended text of EO 12994 that EO 13446 restated, with the restatement disclosed as a change of wording. Section 5 is a fixed-term continuance and is separate from them; its end does not end the amendments, and the amendments do not extend it.
independent_command_check: Each of the five sections is a separate command: section 1 renames, sections 2, 3 and 4 amend different provisions of EO 12994, and section 5 continues the committee for a fixed period. No section depends on another for its force and none carries a condition from the others, so the end of section 5 on 2005-09-30 does not end sections 1 to 4.
savings_check: No clause in the order preserves rights, actions or proceedings, so there is nothing for a revocation or amendment to leave in place; the savings state is none after the bounded search of the held later texts.
